name: Istio
tagline: Routes, secures and observes service traffic through Envoy sidecars, without code changes.

howItWorks.title: Control plane
howItWorks.body:
istiod watches Kubernetes and pushes config to every Envoy over xDS.
It is also the CA: it issues short-lived SPIFFE workload certificates.
If istiod is down, proxies keep serving on cached config and certs.

howItWorks.title: Sidecar injection
howItWorks.body:
A mutating webhook adds istio-proxy to pods at creation.
Set sidecar.istio.io/inject on the pod template annotations.
The namespace needs istio-injection=enabled or a revision label.
Existing pods need a rollout restart to pick up the sidecar.

howItWorks.title: Traffic splitting
howItWorks.body:
DestinationRule names subsets by label: stable and canary.
VirtualService weights split traffic 90/10, 50/50, then 0/100.
Blue-green is the same rule flipped 100/0 to 0/100 in one apply.
ringHash in the DestinationRule hashes a cookie or header for session affinity.

howItWorks.title: Identity and policy
howItWorks.body:
PeerAuthentication STRICT accepts only mTLS between sidecars.
Identity is the certificate, not the IP, so policy survives rescheduling.
AuthorizationPolicy allows by principal, namespace, method and path.
Default-deny first, then allow named service accounts.

howItWorks.title: Multi-cluster
howItWorks.body:
Two clusters share one root CA, a mesh ID and distinct network names.
Remote secrets let each istiod read the other cluster's endpoints.
The east-west gateway is exposed through a NodePort and listens on 15443.
A pod in the receiving cluster takes AUTO_PASSTHROUGH traffic by SNI.

flow: The client calls reviews:9080 as normal.
The sidecar intercepts the outbound connection through iptables redirect.
Envoy matches the host and applies VirtualService route rules.
Weights pick the subset: stable or canary.
DestinationRule applies ringHash, pool limits and outlier detection.
Envoy opens mTLS to the endpoint with its SPIFFE certificate.
The server sidecar checks AuthorizationPolicy and forwards to the app.
For a remote endpoint, traffic goes to the east-west gateway on 15443.

deploy.summary: Bring up nodes, install Istio, split traffic, enforce identity, join a second cluster.
prerequisites: Two Kubernetes clusters with a shared root CA
Linux nodes with sudo and SSH
Cluster 1 node IPs reachable from cluster 2

steps.title: Harden SSH on every node
steps.code:
ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C ops@<HOST> -f ~/.ssh/id_ed25519
ssh-copy-id -i ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub <USER>@<NODE_IP>
printf 'PasswordAuthentication no\nPermitRootLogin no\n' | sudo tee /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/10-harden.conf
sudo sshd -t && sudo systemctl reload ssh
steps.note: Test key login in a second session before reloading. The unit is sshd on RHEL-family hosts.

steps.title: Static address and firewall
steps.code:
# /etc/netplan/50-static.yaml (placeholders)
# network: {version: 2, ethernets: {ens18: {addresses: [<NODE_IP>/24], routes: [{to: default, via: <GW>}], nameservers: {addresses: [<DNS_IP>]}}}}
sudo netplan apply
sudo ufw allow from <PEER_NODE_CIDR> to any port 6443,15443,15012,15017,15021 proto tcp
sudo ufw allow from <PEER_NODE_CIDR> to any port 30000:32767 proto tcp
steps.note: Add DNS A records for the API server and the east-west gateway. Restrict the NodePort range to the peer cluster.

steps.title: Install istioctl and the control plane
steps.code:
curl -L https://istio.io/downloadIstio | ISTIO_VERSION=1.24.1 sh -
cd istio-1.24.1 && export PATH=$PWD/bin:$PATH
istioctl x precheck
istioctl install --set profile=default -y
kubectl -n istio-system get pods
steps.note: On bare metal there is no cloud LoadBalancer, so expose the ingress gateway through a NodePort or MetalLB.

steps.title: Inject the sidecar by annotation
steps.code:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata: {name: frontend-v1, namespace: shop}
spec:
  selector: {matchLabels: {app: frontend, version: v1}}
  template:
    metadata:
      labels: {app: frontend, version: v1}
      annotations:
        sidecar.istio.io/inject: "true"
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: frontend
          image: <REGISTRY>/frontend:1.0.0
steps.note: First run kubectl label namespace shop istio-injection=enabled. Pods must show 2/2 ready.

steps.title: DestinationRule: subsets and ringHash
steps.note: Apply this before the VirtualService. A missing subset returns 503 with NR or UH flags.

steps.title: VirtualService: 90/10 to 0/100
steps.note: Raise canary to 50, then 100, by editing weights. Blue-green is 100/0 flipped to 0/100 in one apply.

steps.title: STRICT mTLS and AuthorizationPolicy
steps.code:
apiVersion: security.istio.io/v1
kind: PeerAuthentication
metadata: {name: default, namespace: shop}
spec: {mtls: {mode: STRICT}}
---
apiVersion: security.istio.io/v1
kind: AuthorizationPolicy
metadata: {name: frontend-allow, namespace: shop}
spec:
  selector: {matchLabels: {app: frontend}}
  action: ALLOW
  rules:
    - from: [{source: {principals: ["cluster.local/ns/istio-system/sa/istio-ingressgateway-service-account"]}}]
      to: [{operation: {methods: ["GET"]}}]
steps.note: Once any ALLOW policy matches a workload, everything else is denied. Confirm meshed clients first.

steps.title: Multi-cluster: two clusters, one mesh
steps.code:
# shared root CA: one cacerts secret per cluster, signed by the same root
kubectl --context $CTX1 -n istio-system create secret generic cacerts --from-file=ca-cert.pem --from-file=ca-key.pem --from-file=root-cert.pem --from-file=cert-chain.pem
kubectl --context $CTX1 label namespace istio-system topology.istio.io/network=network1
# install istiod with global.meshID=mesh1, multiCluster.clusterName=cluster1, network=network1 (cluster2: network2)
./samples/multicluster/gen-eastwest-gateway.sh --network network1 | istioctl --context $CTX1 install -y -f -
kubectl --context $CTX1 -n istio-system patch svc istio-eastwestgateway -p '{"spec":{"type":"NodePort"}}'
kubectl --context $CTX1 apply -n istio-system -f samples/multicluster/expose-services.yaml
istioctl create-remote-secret --context $CTX1 --name cluster1 | kubectl apply -f - --context $CTX2
# repeat with the contexts swapped for cluster2
steps.note: Run on both clusters. expose-services.yaml opens 15443 with AUTO_PASSTHROUGH. Declare the NodePort address under meshNetworks (unverified).

verify: istioctl proxy-status shows every proxy SYNCED.
istioctl x describe pod <frontend-pod> -n shop shows STRICT mTLS and weights.
istioctl remote-clusters lists cluster2 as synced.
Curl frontend from cluster1 repeatedly and watch pods in both clusters answer.
pitfalls: Missing subset in the DestinationRule returns 503 with NR or UH response flags.
STRICT before every client is meshed resets plaintext callers.
Annotation needs the namespace injection label or revision; restart existing pods.
ringHash on a cookie needs clients that keep cookies, or hashing degrades.
Clusters with different root CAs cannot establish cross-cluster mTLS.
A NodePort east-west gateway needs 15443 reachable across clusters on a stable node IP.
Default retries plus your own retries multiply load; set attempts explicitly.
keyPoints: VirtualService and DestinationRule drive canary, blue-green and 90/10 to 0/100 splits.
ringHash consistent hashing pins each user to one frontend pod.
Strict mTLS plus AuthorizationPolicy decide which identity may call what.
Two clusters join one mesh through an east-west gateway on a NodePort.
quickDeploy: Install istioctl and the control plane.
Annotate pod templates for sidecar injection.
Apply DestinationRule subsets, then weighted VirtualService.
osiNote: Envoy proxies L4 and L7: mTLS, routing by header, path and weight.
production: Run two or more istiod replicas with a PodDisruptionBudget.
Pin the Istio version; upgrade with revisions and canary the data plane.
Set explicit timeouts, retries and outlier detection on every hot route.
Keep PERMISSIVE until every client is meshed, then enforce STRICT.
Alert on 5xx rate, request p95 and istioctl proxy-status drift.
